disagreements: Witness 2, the tangential double root: the packet claims (2t−1)² on [0,1] has Bernstein sequence [1.0, 0.0, 1.0]. Computing it myself gives [1.0, −1.0, 1.0] (b0=p(0)=1, b2=p(1)=1, b1 from p(0.5)=0 ⇒ 0.25+0.5·b1+0.25=0 ⇒ b1=−1). The packet's [1.0, 0.0, 1.0] is actually the sequence of 2(t−½)²+½, a polynomial with NO real roots, so returning an empty list for it would be the correct answer, not a silent wrong one. The real (2t−1)² refuses RootNotIsolated because its sequence has v=2 sign changes and subdivides into [1,0,0]/[0,0,1] contact children that drive to the width floor. The test double_root_refuses_never_an_empty_list therefore uses [1.0, −1.0, 1.0], which is the correct Bernstein sequence.

Witness 4, the clustered roots: the packet claims p_s(t)=(t−(0.5−s))(t−(0.5+s)) has Bernstein sequence [0.25−s², −s², 0.25−s²]. Expanding p_s = t²−t+(0.25−s²) and matching coefficients gives the middle coefficient −0.25−s², not −s² (b0=b2=0.25−s²; −2b0+2b1=−1 ⇒ b1=−0.25−s²). The cluster tests therefore use [0.25−s², −0.25−s², 0.25−s²].

Witness 1, the simple root: the packet's p(t)=t−0.5 on [0,1] ([−0.5, 0.5]) puts the root exactly at the dyadic midpoint 0.5. The first bisection at 0.5 then produces children [−0.5, 0] and [0, 0.5], each an endpoint-contact box (v==0 with has_zero) that under decision 0/decision 2 must subdivide to the width floor and refuse — so Ok(v) with 0.5 ∈ v is impossible for this witness on [0,1]. The test uses the same polynomial on domain (0.0, 0.75) with coefficients [−0.5, 0.25]; 0.5 lies at 2/3 of the domain, which is not a dyadic rational, so no bisection boundary ever lands on the root and it isolates cleanly, still containing 0.5.

Cluster half-width s: the packet fixes s = 2⁻¹², whose roots 0.5∓2⁻¹² are dyadic rationals. Bisection of [0,1] reaches the grid point 2⁻¹² exactly, so a bisection boundary lands precisely on the root (the box [2046/4096, 2048/4096] has midpoint 2047/4096 = 0.5−2⁻¹²), producing endpoint-contact children that refuse — the separate test could never return Ok. The tests use s = 0.001 instead: 0.5∓0.001 are not dyadic rationals, so the roots stay strictly interior and separate correctly.

Cluster budget: the packet says budget 32 ≥ log2(1/s)+slack is enough. With tau = 1.0e-6 the real requirement is ~39 subdivisions (initial split plus ~19 refinement levels per root, log2(0.5/1e-6) ≈ 18.9), so 32 is insufficient and would refuse. clustered_roots_separate_with_enough_budget uses budget 64; clustered_roots_refuse_without_enough_budget uses budget 4 (< needed), matching the packet's intent that the two tests differ only by budget.
